body_text: PDF Version PRE Monthly Revenue PRE Monthly Revenue IM8 is the fastest-growing premium supplement brand ever recorded — over 50 million servings delivered to date, with approximately 200,000 servings currently delivered daily, and an order every 27 seconds Prenetics raises full-year 2026 IM8 revenue guidance to $210–220 million, up from $190–210 million IM8 expected to reach $300 million in annualized run-rate revenue by year-end 2026 IM8 expected to deliver $400 million or more in full-year 2027 revenue Every $1 invested in customer acquisition has returned $1.44 in gross profit, blended across all mature cohorts NEW YORK, July 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Prenetics Global Limited (NASDAQ: PRE) (“Prenetics” or the “Company”), a leading consumer health company and parent of the AI-native direct-to-consumer wellness brand IM8, co-founded by David Beckham, today announced the closing of $1 billion in growth financing from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (“CVF”). Under the arrangement, General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund will finance up to 70% of IM8’s marketing spend, with IM8 retaining full discretion over facility utilization. In return, General Catalyst will receive a capped share of income that is tied to the performance of customer cohorts financed through the program, capped at predetermined levels. Once General Catalyst has recovered its investment and capped return on any given monthly cohort, all subsequent value from those customers accrues entirely and permanently to IM8. The arrangement does not involve the issuance of any equity, warrants, or convertible instruments to General Catalyst, and is tracked separately for each monthly cohort of customers. The financing extends Prenetics’ capital-efficient growth strategy. Prenetics enters this partnership from a position of financial strength, with approximately $139.7 million in combined total of estimated cash balances, current financial assets measured at fair value through profit or loss, and cash consideration held in escrow and holdback as of May 31, 2026, and a disciplined balance sheet demonstrated by the $40 million share repurchase program announced earlier in 2026. The rationale for the CVF partnership is structural rather than liquidity-driven. Historically, high-growth consumer businesses have faced a binary choice when scaling customer acquisition: raise dilutive equity capital, or hold back on growth to preserve cash reserves. The Customer Value Fund represents a third way: no-dilution, risk-aligned, cohort-matched capital that is purpose-built to finance customer acquisition and is repaid only from the revenue those customers generate. This allows IM8 to invest more aggressively in brand and marketing—powered by its AI-driven acquisition engine—while preserving Prenetics’ balance sheet for the product innovation, clinical research, and strategic opportunities where its cash is the appropriate funding source. The transformational potential of the arrangement goes beyond removing a cash constraint. IM8's customer acquisition investments have consistently returned multiples of their cost in gross profit over the customer lifetime, and because IM8's customers are subscribers, those returns continue to compound month after month. By financing up to 70% of those investments through cohort-matched capital, the CVF structure materially improves the return on Prenetics’ own cash deployed for customer acquisition and enables IM8 to compound growth without depleting the balance sheet. Every IM8 customer cohort since launch has exceeded the contractual performance thresholds defined in the arrangement, and General Catalyst’s $1 billion commitment reflects rigorous cohort-level diligence: every monthly cohort examined at the transaction level. The $1 billion facility is expected to be deployed across the full breadth of IM8’s sales and marketing investment: digital performance marketing across every major platform, offline and connected-TV media, ambassador and athlete partnerships, brand activations and sponsorships, content production, and retention marketing — in each of IM8’s 43 markets and in the new markets and product categories the brand enters. IM8 operates as an AI-native organization, with artificial intelligence and machine learning embedded across the company, from marketing and merchandising to customer experience and retention. The brand’s acquisition engine runs continuous, automated experimentation at a scale few consumer companies attempt: at any given time, thousands of ads are live and being tested across 43 markets; every landing page, funnel, and website experience is subject to always-on A/B and multivariate testing; and predictive models score cohort quality and customer lifetime value in near real time, governing where the next dollar of acquisition spend goes — the same transaction-level cohort data General Catalyst underwrote in its diligence. This is a machine that compounds in efficiency as data accumulates, and it is the engine through which the CVF capital will be deployed. The structure is designed to preserve Prenetics' financial flexibility: there is no fixed repayment obligation, no maturity date, no financial covenants, and General Catalyst's recovery comes solely from the revenue generated by the funded customer cohorts; repayment simply tracks the revenue those customers produce, with no recourse to Prenetics beyond them. For accounting purposes, and consistent with the accepted treatment of comparable Customer Value Fund arrangements by other publicly traded companies, Prenetics will classify the arrangement as a financial liability on its consolidated balance sheet, with the return component recognized as interest expense below operating income; meaning the arrangement introduces no new operating expense and has no impact on gross margin. 100% of marketing spend will continue to be recorded as sales and marketing expense. Danny Yeung, Chief Executive Officer of Prenetics and Co-Founder of IM8, said: "Nineteen months ago, IM8 was an idea David Beckham and I were building around one belief: that people deserve premium science-backed products they can trust every day. Today it's the fastest-growing premium supplement brand ever recorded , and General Catalyst's $1 billion commitment validates the strength of the cohort economics we've built. Every mature customer cohort since launch has exceeded the performance thresholds General Catalyst diligenced against, cohort after cohort, in the deepest diligence process I've been through as a founder. That is what has led us here. For a year, investors have asked whether we were spending too much on customer acquisition. Now the proof is public: every dollar we have ever spent acquiring customers has already returned $1.44 in gross profit — and that number rises every month, because these are subscribers. The right question was never whether we were spending too much; it’s whether we were spending enough. With this financing we can now accelerate brand and marketing across our 43 countries without issuing a single share to fund it — a structure that keeps every dollar of shareholder value with our shareholders. Our ambition is to build a multi-billion-dollar global consumer health brand. This partnership materially accelerates that path .” “IM8 is a category-defining consumer health business, and the underlying cohort economics are among the strongest we’ve seen across the Customer Value Fund portfolio,” said Adit Swarup, Partner at General Catalyst and lead on the CVF partnership with Prenetics. “Their cohort retention data is remarkable : highly consistent across geographies, subscription tenors, and product lines, with quarterly renewal rates setting new industry benchmarks for direct-to-consumer health. When you combine IM8’s best-in-class unit economics, a repeatable customer acquisition engine across 43 countries, and a founding team led by Danny Yeung with the cultural reach of a co-founder like David Beckham, you have exactly the kind of business the CVF was built to accelerate. We believe this partnership can help solidify IM8 as one of the leading global consumer health brands of the coming decade.” Additional Materials: A detailed investor presentation providing additional context on the transaction, including cohort-level economics, IM8’s business trajectory, and the mechanics of the Customer Value Fund arrangement, is available at www.ir.prenetics.com IM8 is the fastest-growing premium supplement brand ever recorded. Launched in December 2024 in partnership with global icon and co-founder David Beckham, IM8 has scaled from zero to over $200 million in annualized run-rate revenue within its first nineteen months of operations, a pace of category expansion unprecedented in the direct-to-consumer supplement industry. Through just two flagship products: Daily Ultimate Essentials, a 90-ingredient daily nutrition foundation, and Daily Ultimate Longevity, IM8 has delivered over 50 million total servings to customers since launch and is currently delivering approximately 200,000 servings every day and an order every 27 seconds across its 43-country global footprint, with category-leading gross margins and cohort retention metrics. IM8 delivered its strongest month in company history in June 2026, with preliminary unaudited monthly revenue of approximately $17 million, and momentum has continued into the third quarter. Prenetics is raising its full-year 2026 IM8 revenue guidance to $210–220 million, up from $190–210 million previously — its second guidance increase this year. In its second full year of operations, IM8 is expected to reach $300 million in annualized run-rate revenue by year-end 2026, and to deliver in excess of $400 million in full-year 2027 revenue. Prenetics’ long-term ambition is to build IM8 into one of the world’s largest premium consumer health and longevity brands, with a strategic path to billion-dollar scale in annual revenue over the coming years. The brand’s partner and equity-partner roster includes David Beckham, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Aryna Sabalenka, Ollie Bearman, Jay Shetty, and Inter Miami CF. The below chart shows the growth in IM8’s monthly revenue since December 2024 through June 2026. The CVF financing follows a period of significant strategic momentum for Prenetics, including the reclassification of the company as a consumer health business. Following the record scale IM8 has achieved with just its two flagship SKUs, new product launches are planned across Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, including IM8 Hydration in Q4 2026 and a category-first premium gummies line in Q1 2027, meaningfully expanding IM8’s addressable market. IM8 continues to expand its clinical evidence base, with two active randomized controlled trials on gut health and longevity currently underway. IM8 is the fastest-growing premium supplement brand ever recorded, surpassing $200 million in annualized run-rate revenue within 18 months of launch, shipping to 43 countries, and delivering approximately 200,000 servings daily. IM8's ambassador and equity-partner roster includes David Beckham, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Aryna Sabalenka, Ollie Bearman, Jay Shetty, and Inter Miami CF. title: 4 Things To Avoid After Treatment With Jeuveau®
summary: Don’t. Even. Think About It. Let’s set the scene: You scheduled your Jeuveau frown line wrinkle treatment consultation weeks...
body_text: Don’t. Even. Think About It. Let’s set the scene: You scheduled your Jeuveau® frown line wrinkle treatment consultation weeks in advance. With excitement, you check in to your appointment, see your licensed injector, and they treat your unwanted frown lines with expertise and precision. (Read as a refreshed, not frozen look!) Upon leaving the office, you realize you forgot that you have a facial on your calendar for later in the day, and were thinking about taking a workout class, too. You know that your tox results won’t have kicked in yet — so, should you participate in these wellness activities after treatment? According to the experts: No. At least not right away. We went to the pros — Marina Peredo, a board-certified dermatologist in New York City, and Dr. Ariel Ostad, a board certified dermatologist and cosmetic surgeon, to discuss the top four things they recommend avoiding after your tox appointment. No facials It’s true, we love when skin looks its very best (obvi!), and a facial can surely make your epidermis glow. That said, if you’re pining for a facial, you’ll want to schedule it in the days or weeks before you see your injector for Jeuveau®. As for getting a facial after: It’s not recommended. At least not for 24 hours following your injections. In fact, specialists recommend you avoid any other face, neck and head related appointments (including lying face down at the chiropractor) the same day as your treatment. Dr. Ostad says that getting facials, and even going to the dentist, can risk misplacing the neurotoxin, so avoid putting any pressure on the face (this includes your jade roller) — especially the areas that have been treated with tox. No exfoliants, chemicals or scrubs Massaging and rubbing your face is a no-no, but so is applying certain tools and ingredients. “For a few days after your treatment, don’t use any facial treatments such as microdermabrasion or a chemical peel, facial massages (again, no jade roller), exfoliating scrubs or fillers in the treated area,” says Dr. Peredo. It’s important to note: This suggestion isn’t just about treatments and products at doctors’ offices and med spas. Dr. Peredo’s recommends that tox patients are easy on the skin at-home too, post-tox appointment. “When washing your face, be gentle and don’t scrub too hard,” she says. “Keep your face clean especially around the injection sites to reduce the risk of irritation or infection.” No makeup application Perhaps you’re on your way to your injector after just leaving a work meeting — and wearing a full face of makeup. That’s totally OK! Practitioners will remove makeup and sterilize the injection sites before treatment. That said: It’s what you do after the treatment (or should we say, what you don’t do) that counts. Do not apply makeup to the treatment area According to Dr. Peredo, you may have some redness, swelling or very occasional bruising right after the injections. “Sometimes you will see small red bumps that usually disappear soon after the treatment.” In truth, applying makeup can cause more harm (read: potential risk of infection) than (fleeting, cover up) good. So just don’t do it for the rest of the day you get injected. No yoga, no working out Sorry yogis, downward dogs and child poses are banned in the hours after your tox treatment. And no running, HIIT classes or weightlifting either. Although exercise is good for your overall health, it’s not good for your face after injections. Dr. Ostad advises, “Do not exercise or practice yoga until the next day.” We hate to miss a sweat session, but working out immediately after treatment may cause diffusion of the neurotoxin away from injected areas. As a result, this can create unwanted side effects including eyelid droopiness and/or elevated brows. No bending forward Er… What we mean to say is… don’t lean or bend forward until the next day or lay down for a while after getting treatment. Doing so is another way to cause diffusion of the neurotoxin away from the injected areas, says Dr. Ostad. Not only that, taking a snooze — well, laying down (not-so-much the sleeping part) — can lead to inadvertent muscle weakness in undesired areas leading to complications of eyelid droopiness, he says. Now that you have some helpful tips for what not to do after tox, you’re prepared for your treatment. As always, consult with your licensed injector before and after your personalized consultation should you have any questions at all. Need help finding a qualified injector? Jeuveau NEAR ME

title: American Water Announces Quarterly Dividend
body_text: Cash dividend payable in the third quarter of 2026 CAMDEN, N.J. , July 29, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- American Water Works Company, Inc. title: Aurora Launches Second-Generation Driverless Trucks in U.S. to Meet Customer Demand

body_text: Aurora Launches Second-Generation Driverless Trucks in U.S. to Meet Customer Demand July 22, 2026 9:00am EDT Download as PDF Manufacturing partner Roush targeting annual production run-rate of 1,000 trucks by end of year PITTSBURGH--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Aurora Innovation, Inc. (NASDAQ: AUR), the leader in self-driving freight, has launched its second-generation driverless trucks. Aurora plans to deploy the new fleet across its commercial network, which currently encompasses 10 driverless routes throughout the U.S. Sun Belt, to serve additional customers. This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260722856350/en/ Aurora recently launched its second-generation driverless trucks without a person behind the wheel. [Credit: Aurora] Aurora made history when it deployed Class 8 trucks powered by the Aurora Driver, its self-driving system, on public roads last year. As of the end of June, the Aurora Driver has completed nearly 440,000 driverless miles. The company’s route expansion is also driving significant commercial momentum, underscored by a customer's recent plan to purchase 500 Aurora Driver-powered trucks . “Last year’s driverless launch proved our technology could operate safely on public roads – our new platform now provides the foundation to deliver at scale,” said Chris Urmson, CEO and co-founder of Aurora. “Deploying our second-generation truck allows us to put hundreds of autonomous trucks on the road and ultimately into the hands of more customers.” The new fleet, based on the International® LT® Series vehicle, is also powered by Aurora’s next-generation hardware. This hardware is more powerful and built to last one million miles – key factors for deploying at scale. Prior to launch, Aurora closed its Safety Case , its well-established bar for operations on public roads without a person behind the wheel, for the new truck and hardware. Roush, a premier product development supplier, is installing redundant systems and integrating Aurora’s next-generation hardware into the new trucks at a production facility dedicated to Aurora. The companies have also formalized an upfit process, positioning Roush to reach an annual production run-rate of 1,000 Aurora trucks later this year. “By working with a world-class manufacturing partner like Roush, we can meet our customer demand and continue to make the movement of goods safer and more efficient across the country,” added Urmson. Aurora will host a livestream debut of its second-generation driverless trucks on Thursday, July 23 at 3:30 p.m. ET. Sign up to watch at www.aurora.tech/letsroll . About Aurora Aurora (NASDAQ: AUR) is delivering the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly to make transportation safer, increasingly accessible, and more reliable and efficient than ever before. The Aurora Driver is a self-driving system designed to operate multiple vehicle types, from freight-hauling trucks to ride-hailing passenger vehicles, and underpins Aurora’s driver as a service product for trucking. Aurora is working with industry leaders across the transportation ecosystem, including AUMOVIO, FedEx, Hirschbach, McLane, NVIDIA, PACCAR, Ryder, Schneider, Toyota, Uber, Uber Freight, Volvo Trucks, Volvo Autonomous Solutions, and Werner. title: Newmark Facilitates Sale of EmeryTech, Best-in-Class Creative Office in East Bay
summary: Newmark announces the Company has arranged the sale of EmeryTech, a premier creative office campus at 1400 65th Street in Emeryville, California.
body_text: July 24, 2026 12:00 PM Newmark announces the Company has arranged the sale of EmeryTech, a premier creative office campus at 1400 65th Street in Emeryville, California. Executive Vice Chairman and President, Western Region Capital Markets Steve Golubchik , Vice Chairman Edmund Najera and Senior Managing Director Darren Hollak represented buyer Cannae Partners in the transaction. Comprising 234,016 square feet, EmeryTech stands as one of the East Bay’s most distinctive creative offices, featuring 28-foot ceilings, expansive natural light and flexible open floorplates. Benefitting from more than $37.9 million in recent capital improvements, the asset is a highly upgraded workspace with a robust amenity package, including a fitness center, rock-climbing gym, outdoor courtyards and bike facilities. Newmark also represented the undisclosed seller. “EmeryTech checked every box investors are looking for in the East Bay: institutional-quality construction, significant recent capital investment, durable cash flow and a location at the center of the region’s innovation economy,” said Golubchik. “As office fundamentals continue to stabilize, opportunities to acquire a truly differentiated creative campus at a basis well below replacement cost are increasingly difficult to find. Cannae recognized that value and moved decisively.” Located in the heart of Emeryville, EmeryTech offers immediate access to the East Bay, San Francisco and Marin County, while sitting amid a dense collection of retail, dining and life science properties. The campus is also positioned near major employers and research institutions throughout the broader innovation ecosystem that has long-defined Emeryville and Berkeley. The property is currently 66.9% leased and anchored by Premier Nutrition, which recently executed a long-term, 10-year lease. “It is incredibly rare to find a building that combines top-tier advanced manufacturing attributes — like outstanding clear heights, dual power feeds, and heavy floor loads — with a build-out as one of the premier creative office assets in the region, comparable to anything in Palo Alto or San Francisco,” said Bob Basso, Principal at Cannae Partners. “The dearth of quality space across the Bay Area is already driving active tenant interest, and we look forward to aggressively working with the market to fully stabilize the project.” According to Newmark Research , tenants across the East Bay are increasingly gravitating toward high-quality space with existing buildouts. While office vacancy remains elevated, the market is undergoing a pricing reset that is creating new acquisition opportunities for well-capitalized buyers. “The response from the investment community underscored the continued demand for best-in-class office product,” added Hollak. “When a property combines strong tenancy, long-term income, extensive amenities and authentic creative character, capital shows up. EmeryTech attracted interest from a deep pool of institutional and private investors seeking exactly that profile.” About Newmark Newmark Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: NMRK), together with its subsidiaries (“Newmark”), is a world leader in commercial real estate, seamlessly powering every phase of the property life cycle. Newmark’s comprehensive suite of services and products is uniquely tailored to each client, from owners to occupiers, investors to founders, and startups to blue-chip companies. Combining the platform’s global reach with market intelligence in both established and emerging property markets, Newmark provides superior service to clients across the industry spectrum. For the twelve months ended March 31, 2026, Newmark generated revenues of more than $3.4 billion. As of March 31, 2026, Newmark and its business partners together operated from over 185 offices with more than 9,600 professionals across four continents. title: Dental Inventory Management: Vendor Consolidation Strategies
body_text: The best dental vendor consolidation strategies are a structured set of steps that reduce supply costs 15–25% by concentrating purchases with 3–5 primary vendors instead of the 8–12 most practices currently manage. The core approach: audit your current spend, build a clinical formulary, join a dental GPO or negotiate direct volume pricing, and renegotiate contracts annually. Independent practices that implement this framework typically save $47,000–$78,000 per year. The average dental practice maintains relationships with 8 to 12 different suppliers each with its own ordering system, contract cycle, and minimum order threshold. That fragmentation costs more than most practice owners realize: inconsistent pricing, missed volume discount tiers, and dozens of administrative hours every month that belong on patient care, not procurement admin. Dental vendor consolidation strategies give practices, groups, and DSOs a practical path to lower supply costs, cleaner inventory management, and a staff workload that scales without adding headcount. Dental supply vendor consolidation when executed with a structured framework unlocks pricing leverage that fragmented purchasing simply cannot reach. This guide walks through the seven-step consolidation framework used by high-performing practices in 2026 from the initial spend audit through formulary building, GPO participation, and annual contract review cycles. Most dental practices manage 8–12 vendors more than they need. Consolidating to 3–5 primary suppliers through GPO participation, formulary standardization, and annual contract renegotiation typically cuts supply costs by 15–25% and frees 3–5 staff hours per week. This guide covers all seven steps, from the initial spend audit to annual contract renewal cycles. Key Takeaways Target supply costs below 8% of collections dental supplies typically account for 5–8% of collections ( ZenOne ), and vendor consolidation is one of the fastest levers for reducing total overhead below 60% GPO participation delivers measurable savings quickly independent practices save 15–25% on supplies through group purchasing organizations, with average annual savings ranging from $47,000 to $78,000 ( Private Dental Alliance ) Build your formulary before negotiating without a standardized clinical formulary, supplier negotiations lack the volume data to move pricing in your favor DSO formulary standardization unlocks scale advantages without it, each location negotiates independently and collective purchasing power disappears into fragmented SKU counts Renegotiate vendor contracts every 12 months supply costs have risen steadily since 2020; practices that haven't reviewed contracts recently are likely paying more than necessary Staff bandwidth is a hidden cost of vendor fragmentation every hour managing vendor portals and rep calls is an hour not available for patient scheduling, call follow-up, or case acceptance AI receptionists offset front desk bandwidth loss Arini's AI receptionist handles patient calls 24/7, freeing staff to focus on strategic procurement tasks without sacrificing appointment capture or patient communication What Are Dental Vendor Consolidation Strategies? Dental vendor consolidation strategies are structured approaches for reducing a dental practice's active supplier relationships typically from 8–12 vendors down to 3–5 primary suppliers. Concentrating purchasing volume with fewer vendors unlocks better pricing tiers, simplified ordering, and stronger service commitments that fragmented supply chains cannot achieve. Most practices save 15–25% on supply costs after consolidation. Dental Vendor Consolidation: 7-Step Framework Audit your current vendor spend - Collect 12 months of purchasing data across all vendors and portals to establish a spend baseline Segment suppliers by strategic value - Classify each vendor by annual spend and clinical criticality (strategic, leverage, bottleneck, routine) Build a clinical formulary - Standardize approved products by category before entering any vendor negotiations Join a dental GPO or negotiate volume pricing - Use consolidated spend to unlock tiered discounts unavailable to individual practices Free up staff bandwidth - Reduce procurement administrative workload so patient coverage and supply management don't compete Automate reordering and PMS integration - Set par levels and configure automated purchase orders tied to usage data Review and renegotiate vendor contracts annually - Sustain savings through a consistent annual contract review cycle Most dental practices accumulate vendor relationships without a deliberate strategy. A distributor rep signs the practice up for composites. Another handles PPE. Lab services, imaging consumables, and sterilization supplies each have separate accounts. Within a few years, the average practice is managing 8 to 12 separate vendor relationships each requiring its own login, ordering cycle, and rep communication. Consolidation doesn't mean choosing one vendor for everything. It means making deliberate decisions about which vendor categories to consolidate, which relationships to preserve for clinical or strategic reasons, and how to concentrate purchasing volume into pricing leverage. The goal of dental vendor consolidation is a smaller, more strategic vendor set where: Each supplier handles a meaningful portion of total annual spend Contract terms reflect actual volume, not generic rack pricing Administrative workload reduces to a predictable weekly cadence Supply data is clean and consistent enough to support ongoing negotiation For DSOs and multi-location dental groups , vendor consolidation also creates the data infrastructure for formulary compliance reporting, cross-location spend analysis, and centralized procurement governance. Why Vendor Fragmentation Costs More Than You Think The most visible cost of vendor fragmentation is pricing when spend is spread across too many suppliers, no single vendor sees enough volume to justify tiered discounts or priority service. But the pricing gap is only part of the overhead picture. The Administrative Time Cost Managing 10+ vendor relationships requires recurring staff time that rarely appears on any cost report. The weekly touchpoints add up quickly: Checking 4–8 ordering portals and submitting separate orders for each Fielding calls and emails from multiple sales reps Matching invoices to purchase orders across different systems and formats Chasing backorders, verifying product substitutions, and updating par levels per vendor Training staff on multiple ordering platforms as turnover occurs In most dental practices, front desk staff and office managers split time between patient-facing work and supply management without a dedicated procurement role. Every hour spent on vendor portals or rep calls is an hour not available for appointment scheduling, insurance verification, or patient communication. The Pricing Inconsistency Cost Fragmented purchasing makes price comparison nearly impossible. When gloves come from three different distributors at different unit prices under different contract structures, there's no clean baseline for negotiation and no leverage to demand better terms from any individual vendor. Supply costs have risen steadily since 2020 as manufacturers pass along raw material and shipping expenses ( ZenOne ). Practices without current volume-based contracts are most exposed to those increases. Practices with consolidated spend and negotiated pricing caps manage the exposure far better. The Compliance and Tracking Burden Multi-location groups and DSOs face an additional layer of risk from fragmented vendor management: Inconsistent product standards across locations complicate quality tracking Expiration date management spans multiple supplier timelines and delivery schedules Without a shared formulary, clinical staff make independent purchasing decisions that undermine collective volume Pro Tip: Before starting any consolidation initiative, calculate your current supply spend as a percentage of collections. National benchmarks put supply costs at 5–8% of collections. Anything above 8% warrants an immediate vendor audit. Step 1: Audit Your Current Vendor Spend Consolidation starts with accurate data. Before approaching any vendor about pricing or contract terms, you need a clear picture of what you're buying, from whom, and at what price. Gather 12 months of supply purchasing data from: All active vendor portals and ordering platforms Credit card statements (many dental supply purchases occur outside formal PO systems) Accounts payable records and invoices Practice management software purchasing modules, if available Key metrics to pull from that data: Metric What It Reveals Total spend by vendor Which vendors get the most money and which ones should. SKU count per vendor Whether you're buying too many variants of the same product. Order frequency per vendor Which vendors are truly operational vs. ad hoc. Spend concentration What percentage of spend goes to your top 3 vendors. Expired/wasted inventory Whether par levels and order quantities are calibrated to actual usage. Most practices are surprised by what the audit surfaces. Common findings include: 60–70% of spend is concentrated in 2–3 vendors , with a long tail of small-spend suppliers that receive disproportionate administrative attention Duplicate SKUs the same product ordered from multiple vendors at different price points Significant overstock on slow-moving items that inflated past orders Ordering patterns driven by rep relationships rather than clinical need or price comparison This audit gives you the foundation for every consolidation decision that follows. Complete it before any supplier conversations begin. Step 2: Segment Suppliers by Strategic Value Not all vendor relationships warrant the same level of investment. A structured segmentation approach adapted from supply chain management for dental practice context divides current vendors into four categories based on two dimensions: annual spend and clinical criticality . Segment Spend Criticality Consolidation Strategy Strategic High High Deepen the relationship; negotiate multi-year contracts with service and fill-rate commitments. Leverage High Low Consolidate aggressively; these commodity items respond directly to volume pricing. Bottleneck Low High Maintain backup sources; clinical risk from stockout outweighs pricing opportunity. Routine Low Low Consolidate or eliminate; shift to the primary distributor if the product is available there. Typical examples of each quadrant in a dental practice: Strategic: Lab services (crown and bridge, implants, dentures) high spend, clinical outcomes tied directly to lab quality and turnaround time Leverage: PPE, gloves, masks, disposables high-volume commodity items where pricing is the primary differentiator and alternatives are abundant Bottleneck: Sterilizer replacement parts, niche implant components, specialty clinical materials hard to substitute, essential when needed Routine: Office supplies, printer cartridges, reception area items easily consolidated through a primary distributor without clinical risk Once segmented, your consolidation focus is clear: pursue leverage and routine segments first. These categories offer the fastest cost reduction with the least clinical disruption. Strategic vendors get relationship investment and long-term contract structure. Bottleneck vendors get careful management and documented backup sources not aggressive price negotiation. Step 3: Build a Clinical Formulary A clinical formulary is your practice's approved product catalog the defined list of specific products and brands that clinical staff are authorized to use and order. Without a formulary, individual clinicians default to personal preferences, ordering patterns fragment across dozens of SKUs, and purchasing volume never concentrates enough to drive pricing. Formulary building is the prerequisite for meaningful vendor negotiation. A formulary gives you the volume data vendors need to offer tiered pricing, and it gives your practice the compliance structure to actually capture those tiers. For Solo Practices and Small Groups Building a formulary for a solo or small group practice is straightforward: List all current clinical products by category composites, cements, bonding agents, anesthetics, imaging supplies, sterilization materials, impression materials, PPE For each category, identify the 1–2 products that meet clinical standards after team review Document approved products with specific SKUs in a shared reference list accessible to anyone who orders supplies Standardize ordering non-formulary purchases require sign-off from the practice owner or office manager Clinical formulary standardization doesn't restrict clinical decisions it creates predictable, concentrated purchasing around approved products. Where clinically equivalent alternatives exist at meaningfully lower cost often in PPE and commodity categories build the formulary around the value option. Pro Tip: Many generic-equivalent dental consumables meet the same clinical standards as premium branded versions at 20–30% lower cost. Pilot alternatives in a low-stakes category first, validate clinical acceptance, then expand to the formulary. For DSOs and Multi-Location Groups For DSOs, formulary standardization is the most critical step in the entire consolidation process. Without it, each location negotiates independently, collective purchasing volume is never leveraged, and pricing gains disappear into fragmented SKU counts. Effective DSO formulary management requires four structural elements: A clinical review board a cross-functional team of clinical and operational leaders who evaluate and approve products before formulary inclusion A dual-track approval process commodity products (PPE, disposables) standardize through procurement; clinical products require clinical evaluation and doctor sign-off A central product catalog accessible to all locations, with approved SKUs, preferred vendors, and par level guidance by practice type Compliance reporting monthly tracking of which locations are ordering outside the formulary, with root-cause analysis for persistent outliers Without formulary compliance enforcement, a DSO with 20 locations can accumulate 200+ active SKUs in a single product category across the network making volume negotiation mathematically impossible. Clean formulary data is what transforms a collection of locations into a single negotiating entity. Step 4: Join a Dental GPO or Negotiate Volume Pricing With a formulary in place and spend data in hand, you have two primary routes to better pricing. Most practices benefit from pursuing both simultaneously. Option A: Join a Dental Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) A dental GPO aggregates purchasing volume from hundreds or thousands of member practices to negotiate pre-contracted rates with major distributors and manufacturers. Member practices buy at rates that reflect collective volume not individual practice spend. Quantified GPO benefits for dental practices: Independent practices typically save 15–25% on supply costs through GPO membership ( Private Dental Alliance ) Average annual savings for GPO members range from $47,000 to $78,000 A practice spending $5,000–$10,000 per month on supplies can expect $1,500–$3,000 in monthly savings Multi-location groups and DSOs consolidating through a GPO can save $150,000 or more annually GPOs take no ownership stake in member practices and have no influence over clinical decisions. For independent dental practices and small groups that lack the individual volume to move vendor pricing meaningfully, dental GPO consolidation is typically the single highest-return procurement action available and the fastest path to meaningful savings without requiring a large individual spend base. What to evaluate when selecting a dental GPO: Coverage of your formulary products GPO contracts must align with your approved products for savings to materialize Distributor network which major distributors are contracted? Reporting tools can you see spend by category and vendor? Membership cost versus projected savings most dental GPOs are free or nominal cost; verify net savings before committing Option B: Direct Volume Negotiation with Primary Vendors Larger groups and DSOs with sufficient individual volume may find that direct negotiation with primary distributors or manufacturers outperforms GPO pricing at high spend thresholds. Key negotiation leverage points: Total annual spend commitment project 12 months forward, not just current spend Multi-year commitment in exchange for locked pricing or guaranteed increase caps Formulary exclusivity committing your approved SKUs to a single vendor in exchange for tiered pricing Payment terms net-30 or net-45 in exchange for volume commitments Targets for a strong vendor contract: Volume discount tiers (e.g., 10% at $X annual spend, 15% at $2X) Backorder priority and guaranteed fill rate commitments (95%+ is reasonable to request) Dedicated account management with direct escalation access Annual price increase caps, typically 3–5% Quarterly business review meetings to track performance and flag issues GPO vs. Direct Negotiation: Side-by-Side Comparison Factor Dental GPO Direct Vendor Negotiation Best for Independent practices and small groups DSOs and large groups with $1M+ annual spend Typical savings 15–25% on supply costs 20–30% at high-volume thresholds Setup time 30–60 days to activate 60–120 days for contract negotiation Membership cost Free or nominal ($0–$500/year) No membership cost Volume requirement None; GPO pools collective spend across members Requires sufficient individual spend to move vendor pricing Clinical autonomy Fully preserved; no ownership stake Fully preserved; volume commitment only Best first move Yes, for most independent practices After GPO baseline is established, as volume scales Step 5: Free Up Staff Bandwidth for Strategic Procurement One of the most underestimated benefits of vendor consolidation is the recaptured staff time and what practices do with that time determines whether consolidation compounds into long-term operational improvement or remains a one-time cost reduction. The Staff Bandwidth Problem in Dental Procurement In most dental practices, supply management is distributed across the front desk and clinical staff without a dedicated procurement role. The result: Office managers split time between patient calls, scheduling, and supply ordering without enough capacity to do either well Clinical staff interrupt chair-side workflows to handle backorders or substitution decisions Nobody comprehensively owns the vendor relationship, so pricing and service quality drift without accountability Consolidating to 2–4 primary vendors significantly reduces the weekly administrative load of procurement. Ordering cycles become predictable. Rep relationships are fewer and more manageable. Invoice matching is simpler. The staff time freed up can shift to higher-value tasks: verifying insurance before appointments, following up on unsigned treatment plans, or managing the appointment schedule . But there's a real tension here: during the consolidation initiative itself audits, formulary reviews, vendor negotiations staff attention peaks at exactly the moment patient communication needs coverage. Maintaining Call Coverage During Procurement Initiatives When office staff direct time toward supply management tasks spend audits, formulary reviews, contract comparisons patient-facing call coverage suffers. In practices without a dedicated front desk team, this trade-off is real: time on the vendor portal is time off the phones. Arini's AI receptionist answers every patient call in 300 milliseconds, books appointments directly into OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon, and other practice management systems, and handles after-hours inquiries without staff involvement fully HIPAA compliant. When your team is heads-down on an annual vendor audit or contract negotiation cycle, patient calls still get answered and appointment slots still get filled. Together, vendor consolidation and AI receptionist deployment create a compounding overhead reduction: Fewer vendor relationships → less staff time on procurement administration each week AI receptionist coverage → no missed patient calls during high-focus procurement periods Better scheduling fill rates → consistent revenue capture regardless of what operational task staff are working on Kare Mobile captured $56,000 in new patient appointments in month one after deploying Arini without adding front desk headcount. Unified Dental Care increased revenue by 12% after deployment. That revenue capture is what makes the overhead math on both procurement improvement and AI coverage compound simultaneously. Step 6: Automate Reordering and PMS Integration Manual reordering is one of the primary sources of both overstock and stockout events in dental practices. Without automated triggers tied to actual usage data, reordering depends on someone physically noticing that a supply is running low which is inconsistent, error-prone, and creates unnecessary urgency. Automated reordering best practices: Set par levels for every formulary item the minimum on-hand quantity that triggers a reorder. Par levels should reflect 2–3 weeks of typical usage, not historical order quantities Configure purchase order automation within your primary vendor's platform or a dedicated dental inventory management tool, so orders generate when inventory drops below par Review and adjust par levels quarterly usage patterns shift with changes in the schedule, procedure mix, or patient volume Track inventory by operatory , not just by practice, for multi-operatory practices where consumption varies by station What to prioritize when evaluating dental inventory management software: Integration with your PMS usage data from scheduled procedures should inform supply planning Multi-location visibility for groups and DSOs Single-interface ordering across multiple vendors (consolidates the ordering experience even where multiple vendors remain) Expiration date tracking and first-in, first-out enforcement Spend analytics by category, vendor, location, and time period Confirming PMS compatibility before selecting any inventory management software prevents costly mid-implementation surprises Arini's dental PMS integration guide covers OpenDental, EagleSoft, Denticon, and 10+ other platforms. Practices already integrated with Arini's AI receptionist benefit from scheduling data that flows into the PMS in real time as patient calls come in meaning the procedure-level signals that inform supply planning stay current as the schedule fills, not just at week's end. Step 7: Review and Renegotiate Vendor Contracts Annually Vendor consolidation is not a one-time project it's a recurring management cycle. Practices that consolidate once and don't revisit contracts typically lose pricing gains within 12–18 months through incremental price increases, formulary drift, and shifting usage patterns. Annual vendor contract review checklist: [ ] Review spend vs. contracted tiers are you hitting the volume thresholds that unlock discount pricing? [ ] Audit SKU creep have non-formulary products been ordered? If so, address compliance or update the formulary [ ] Benchmark current pricing get competitive quotes or check current GPO rates on core SKUs [ ] Evaluate fill rate and service performance backorder frequency, delivery accuracy, and rep responsiveness are all negotiation leverage [ ] Identify further consolidation opportunities can any secondary vendors be absorbed by a primary relationship? [ ] Review contract expiration dates start renegotiation 60–90 days before expiration, not after When to renegotiate mid-cycle: Patient volume or location count increases significantly, raising supply spend above contracted tiers A vendor raises prices beyond the cap in your current agreement A new GPO contract or distributor promotion offers meaningfully better pricing on core SKUs Service performance (fill rate, delivery, accuracy) drops below contracted commitments The annual review cycle also surfaces new consolidation opportunities. As your formulary matures and usage patterns stabilize, categories that previously required two vendors often consolidate to one compounding savings from the original effort. A mature dental vendor management strategy treats these annual reviews as the core operating cadence part of the broader shift toward proactive dental practice management rather than reactive, one-time projects. DSO-Specific Vendor Consolidation Considerations Dental support organizations and multi-location groups face both greater savings potential and greater organizational complexity in vendor consolidation. Scale amplifies every dynamic including the failure modes. The Formulary Compliance Problem at Scale For a DSO with 10, 20, or 50+ locations, the primary risk of vendor consolidation is formulary non-compliance at the location level. If individual locations continue ordering outside approved SKUs even at low rates the volume concentration that drives pricing breaks down. Addressing compliance at scale: Make the formulary the default configure ordering platforms so formulary items appear first in search results Require written justification for non-formulary orders not to block them, but to create visibility and data for quarterly review Track compliance by location monthly alongside production and collection metrics Use compliance data in leadership conversations treat supply cost efficiency like any other performance metric Centralized vs. Decentralized Procurement Models DSOs typically operate one of three procurement structures: Model Description Best For Centralized Corporate procurement team manages all vendor contracts and ordering. DSOs with 10+ standardized locations. Decentralized Each location manages its own procurement within corporate GPO or contract guardrails. Early-stage DSOs or practices with specialized clinical requirements. Hybrid Corporate sets formulary and contracts; locations execute ordering within those parameters. Most common; balances pricing leverage with local operational flexibility. Most growing DSOs adopt the hybrid model. It provides centralized pricing leverage while allowing locations to manage day-to-day ordering without requiring corporate approval for every purchase. Volume Leverage at the DSO Level A DSO's primary pricing advantage is collective purchasing volume. A 20-location DSO spending $6,000–$8,000 per location per month represents $1.4M–$1.9M in annual supply spend a volume level that qualifies for enterprise-tier pricing with major distributors and manufacturers. DSO procurement priorities: Negotiate at the DSO level , not the location level individual location spend rarely crosses enterprise pricing thresholds Require location-level spend reporting to maintain accurate total volume data for annual negotiations Revisit GPO membership as volume grows GPO pricing that made sense for a 5-location group may be less competitive than a direct manufacturer agreement at 15–20+ locations Unified Dental Care demonstrates this compounding effect in practice: by pairing supply-side efficiency with AI-assisted patient communication, the group achieved a 12% revenue increase and 24% profit increase proof that procurement consolidation and revenue capture reinforce each other at the DSO level. Common Vendor Consolidation Mistakes Even well-structured consolidation initiatives underperform or stall. These are the most frequent failure points: Consolidating before building the formulary moving to fewer vendors before standardizing products means concentrating pricing without controlling volume. Savings are limited and data remains messy. Choosing the lowest price over fill rate the cheapest vendor isn't useful if backorders are frequent. Clinical disruptions from stockouts cost more than modest price premiums on reliable supply. Eliminating bottleneck suppliers too aggressively specialty items with limited alternatives need careful management. Consolidating primary distributors is smart; eliminating your only source for a critical clinical product creates risk you'll discover during a busy clinical day. Ignoring SKU creep after year one formularies erode over time as one-off ordering decisions add new products "just this once." Without periodic audits, compliance drifts and volume leverage shrinks. Not tracking service performance alongside pricing GPO pricing and volume discounts don't matter if your primary vendor's fill rate or delivery accuracy declines. Monitor both. Treating consolidation as a completed project vendor consolidation is an ongoing management discipline. Annual reviews are the mechanism that makes initial savings compound. Underestimating the staff time cost of the initiative itself the audit, formulary build, and negotiation phases are time-intensive. Ensure staff have bandwidth to manage procurement strategically and that patient-facing coverage doesn't suffer during those periods. Final Verdict Dental vendor consolidation isn't a one-size-fits-all process. The right starting point depends on your practice's size, current vendor structure, and where the largest overhead inefficiency lives right now. For independent practices and small groups GPO participation is the highest-ROI first move. It's free or near-free to join, delivers 15–25% savings without requiring the individual volume needed for direct negotiation, and can start generating returns within 30–60 days of activation. For DSOs and multi-location groups build the formulary before everything else. Without formulary compliance, collective purchasing volume never concentrates and pricing leverage at the DSO level never materializes regardless of how many locations you operate. For practices with high administrative overhead address staff bandwidth before renegotiating contracts. Vendor consolidation recaptures 3–5 hours per week of procurement time, but during the audit and negotiation phases, patient communication still needs consistent coverage. Arini's AI receptionist answers calls 24/7 so procurement-focused work periods don't translate into missed bookings or dropped revenue. For practices with aging vendor contracts start with the spend audit. Contracts more than 18 months old likely contain pricing that no longer reflects current volume a structured audit routinely surfaces $10,000–$20,000+ in immediate renegotiation opportunities, before any structural consolidation begins. If your primary goal is reducing supply costs without a major operational overhaul, GPO membership plus a basic clinical formulary is the fastest path to meaningful, compounding savings. Frequently Asked Questions What are the benefits of dental vendor consolidation? Dental vendor consolidation reduces supply costs by 15–25%, simplifies procurement by concentrating ordering into fewer portals, and frees 3–5 staff hours per week from vendor management tasks. Secondary benefits include stronger service commitments from vendors receiving higher volumes, cleaner spend data that strengthens annual renegotiation leverage, and a formulary compliance infrastructure that scales with practice or DSO growth. How do you consolidate dental vendors? To consolidate dental vendors, begin by auditing 12 months of purchasing data to identify which vendors receive the most spend and which categories overlap. Build a clinical formulary to standardize approved products by category, then join a dental GPO or negotiate volume-based contracts directly with primary distributors. The process typically takes 60–90 days and generates measurable savings within the first full contract cycle. What is a dental formulary and why does it matter? A dental formulary is an approved product catalog a defined list of specific products and brands that clinical staff are authorized to order. Formularies matter for vendor consolidation because they concentrate purchasing volume onto defined SKUs. Without a formulary, spend fragments across too many products and vendors cannot offer meaningful volume-based pricing. Building the formulary before vendor negotiations is the step that makes pricing leverage possible. What is dental vendor consolidation? Dental vendor consolidation is the process of intentionally reducing the number of active supplier relationships a practice maintains, concentrating purchasing volume with fewer vendors to achieve better pricing, simplified ordering, and stronger service commitments. Rather than distributing spend across 10+ suppliers, consolidated practices work with 2–5 primary vendors that handle the majority of their supply categories. How many vendors should a dental practice keep? Most well-managed solo and small group practices operate effectively with 3–5 primary vendors: one or two major distributors covering clinical supplies, a lab partner for prosthetics and fixed work, and a specialty vendor for items not covered by primary distributors. The target isn't a specific number it's ensuring every remaining vendor relationship represents meaningful annual spend and strategic value worth managing. How much does dental vendor consolidation save? Savings vary by practice size and starting point. Independent practices that join a dental GPO typically reduce supply costs by 15–25%. Optimized inventory management saves dental professionals an average of $17,000 annually, according to practice data from dental procurement platforms ( ZenOne ). For DSOs and multi-location groups pursuing full consolidation formulary standardization, GPO participation, and direct volume negotiation annual savings can exceed $150,000 per year. What is a dental GPO and is it right for my practice? A dental group purchasing organization (GPO) aggregates purchasing volume from hundreds or thousands of member practices to negotiate pre-contracted pricing with distributors and manufacturers. GPOs are free or low-cost to join and take no ownership stake in member practices, preserving full clinical autonomy. GPOs are a strong fit for independent practices and small groups that lack the individual volume to negotiate meaningful discounts directly. DSOs with high per-location spend may find that direct manufacturer agreements outperform GPO pricing once collective volume crosses enterprise thresholds. Should a DSO build a central formulary before joining a GPO? Yes in almost every case, formulary building should precede or run concurrent with GPO evaluation. A GPO's pricing advantage only materializes when purchases concentrate on formulary-approved products that match the GPO's contracted items. Without formulary alignment, purchases remain fragmented across too many SKUs and GPO contract rates are never actually captured at the spend volumes required for meaningful savings. How does vendor consolidation affect front desk staff time? Fewer vendors mean fewer ordering portals, fewer rep communications, fewer invoices to match, and fewer backorder situations to resolve. For most practices, consolidating vendor relationships through a GPO saves practice managers 3–5 hours per week on vendor management ( Private Dental Alliance ). However, the audit, formulary-building, and negotiation phases require significant upfront staff investment. During those periods, practices where front desk staff manage both procurement and call coverage may experience patient communication gaps. Arini's AI receptionist handles patient calls, appointment scheduling, and after-hours inquiries 24/7, ensuring that procurement-focused work periods don't translate into missed calls or dropped bookings. What should practices do with time freed by consolidation? Consolidating vendors typically frees 3–5 staff hours per week from procurement tasks ordering portal management, rep communications, invoice matching, and backorder resolution. The highest-value uses for that recovered time are front desk revenue activities: scheduling follow-up for unsigned treatment plans, insurance verification before appointments, and returning missed patient calls before they book elsewhere. For practices where front desk staff already split time between calls and clinical operations, Arini's AI receptionist handles inbound patient calls 24/7 freeing that same staff bandwidth for strategic procurement work rather than reactive call coverage. Normandy Lake Dental now answers 90% of patient calls without missing a scheduling opportunity. The combination compounds: vendor consolidation reduces supply costs, while AI call handling captures revenue that fragmented staffing would otherwise miss. Conclusion and Next Steps Dental vendor consolidation is not a complicated strategy but it is a disciplined one. The practices and DSOs that sustain meaningful supply cost reductions do so through a repeatable annual cycle: audit spend, standardize the formulary, concentrate purchasing volume, leverage that volume for better pricing, and review results each year. Dental supplies account for 5–8% of collections, supply costs have risen steadily since 2020, and GPO participation delivers 15–25% savings for independent practices. A practice spending $80,000 annually on supplies that consolidates effectively and joins a GPO can realistically reduce that number to $60,000–$68,000 a recurring improvement that compounds year over year as contracts are renegotiated and compliance matures. Operationally, the case is equally strong. Staff time is finite. Every hour managing 12 vendor portals is an hour not available for patient care, scheduling follow-up, or revenue cycle work. Vendor consolidation recaptures that time and Arini's AI receptionist ensures the time gets invested in strategic work rather than simply filling a different gap in patient coverage.
